- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to sentiment shifts — if sentiment flips from +0.5 to -0.3, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and smooth transition.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 5+ days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) prices; apply 1–2% downward correction for final 5–7 days of forecast.
